_comment: Mutation gate: the nine targets of the core — src/modules/graph.ts (graph resolution), src/runner/dispatch.ts (the order within a point), src/config/history.ts, src/determinism/cbor.ts, src/determinism/digest.ts, src/helpers/height-versioned.ts, src/helpers/cursor-table.ts, src/backbone/core-ledger-state/run-reclaim.ts (the reclamation, in the place of the per-block step src/backbone/core-ledger-state/refcount.ts, which a later change moved to the tests as their reference, as the step had taken the place of the sweep, src/backbone/core-ledger-state/sweep.ts) and src/backbone/core-block-fetch/node-source.ts (the block fetch queue) — each with its fast tests in vitest.mutation.config.ts (perTest coverage reruns only a mutant's covering tests). 0.9.5's five durability adapters were retired with their parts. break stays at 65 on the aggregate over valid mutants (scripts/mutation-per-adapter.mjs runs one stryker run per target); it ratchets up and MUST NOT be lowered to pass. MEASURED BASELINE 2026-10-27 (npm run test:mutation:ci on a loaded machine, load average 25-45, about 58 min in all): graph 87.81% (837 valid, 1068s), dispatch 95.80% (143, 62s), history 86.10% (597, 37s), cbor 98.18% (603, 494s), digest 96.05% (76, 183s), height-versioned 74.07% (54, 66s), cursor-table 78.38% (37, 59s), sweep 60.62% (325, 42s; 79 mutants no-coverage from its one unit test file), node-source 77.80% (491, 1446s; 121 timeouts) => AGGREGATE 85.33% over 3163 valid mutants (2554 killed, 145 timeout, 373 survived, 91 no coverage). REMEASURED 2026-10-28 (the sweep given its tables test, about 41 min): graph 87.80%, dispatch 95.80%, history 85.81%, cbor 96.85%, digest 96.05%, height-versioned 74.07%, cursor-table 78.38%, sweep 90.33% (300 valid), node-source 77.48% => AGGREGATE 87.98% over 3162 valid mutants (2651 killed, 131 timeout, 361 survived, 19 no coverage). MEASURED 2026-11-03 (refcount.ts alone through MUTATION_ADAPTERS, about 6 min): refcount 92.17% (332 valid: 299 killed, 7 timeout, 26 survived, 0 no coverage), the step's two unit tests covering 100% of its lines and branches. MEASURED 2026-11-18 (run-reclaim.ts alone, concurrency 3, on a laptop): 1011 mutants. With its unit tests, its negative controls, its generated histories at 120 a case and its PostgreSQL and PGlite tables test, the dry run took 46 s locally and 88 s on CI, nearly every mutant reran all of them, and CI cancelled the job at its 120 min limit (about 60 min projected locally for this target). Now its unit tests (with writeNet's statements), its negative controls and its generated histories at 10 a case (set by the env of vitest.mutation.config.ts; the normal suite runs them at 120 a case, and runs the tables test): dry run 62 tests in 5 s, the whole target 7 min 15 s locally (about 13.5 min projected on CI), run-reclaim 80.71% (1011 valid: 805 killed, 11 timeout, 187 survived, 8 no coverage; 81.36% of the covered). With unit tests for the survivors that are not equivalent (the reads each step asks for, the key and block a halt names, damaged tables): dry run 72 tests in 5 s, the whole target 6 min 9 s locally (about 11.5 min projected on CI), run-reclaim 92.88% (1011 valid: 928 killed, 11 timeout, 71 survived, 1 no coverage), each of the 72 left equivalent, run only under a negative control's fault, or different only on damaged tables.
